LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do pictures help us to write?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signed vocabulary related to the theme.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify words with the target letter sounds /e /, / iː/, /ea/,/iː/ in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. sign read sentences in a text accurately, at the right speed and with the right facial expression for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of fluency in reading. • In pairs, learners are guided to sign read vocabularies related to living together. • In pairs, learners are guided to identify, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to living together • In groups, learners are guided to listen to and observe short signed paragraphs and point out and fingerspell words with the target letter sounds; /e /, / iː/, /ea/,/iː/. • In pairs, learners are guided to sign read words with the target letter sounds correctly. • Individually,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and Imagination: The learner explores as they create sentences from pictures, with peers and sign

them.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self-esteem is enhanced as learners express oneself effectively through writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Guided writing is practised in Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language.
